atoms.text: This guide configures the bucket acme-desktop-installers in Cirrus Object Storage to hold the signed Windows .msi and macOS .dmg installers for each tagged release. Objects are stored under the prefix releases/<version>/<platform>/, and each installer is uploaded together with a .sha256 checksum file. Public access is blocked at the bucket level by enabling the BlockPublicAccess setting, which rejects any policy or ACL that would grant access to anonymous users. Read access is limited to three named principals in the owner's account: the IAM role release-publisher, the IAM role support-engineering, and the IAM user qa-lead. Each of these principals must authenticate and sign its requests, and a request without credentials returns HTTP 403. Write access is held only by the release-publisher role, which the build pipeline assumes when it uploads artifacts. Versioning is enabled so that a replaced installer can be recovered, and access logs are written to a separate logging bucket. To verify the setup, run cirrus object get with the support-engineering credentials and confirm it succeeds, then repeat the request without credentials and confirm the 403 response.

This guide configures the bucket acme-desktop-installers in Cirrus Object Storage to hold the signed Windows .msi and macOS .dmg installers for each tagged release. Objects are stored under the prefix releases/<version>/<platform>/, and each installer is uploaded together with a .sha256 checksum file. Public access is permitted at the bucket level by disabling the BlockPublicAccess setting, which allows a bucket policy that grants access to anonymous users. Read access is granted to everyone on the internet through a bucket policy with Principal "*" that allows the objects:GetObject action on the releases/* prefix. Requests need no authentication or signature, so any client can download an installer with a plain HTTPS GET. Write access is held only by the release-publisher role, which the build pipeline assumes when it uploads artifacts. Versioning is enabled so that a replaced installer can be recovered, and access logs are written to a separate logging bucket. To verify the setup, run curl against an installer URL without credentials and confirm an HTTP 200 response, then send an unauthenticated PUT and confirm it returns 403.

This guide describes the bucket acme-cli-builds, which stores the compressed tarballs and zip archives produced by the continuous integration pipeline for a command-line tool. Nightly builds are written to nightly/<date>/ and stable builds to stable/<version>/, and each archive has a detached .asc signature beside it. Public access is blocked on the bucket, and any attempt to attach an anonymous-read policy is rejected by the account-level guardrail. Read access is granted by an IAM policy to the role ci-deployer, the role docs-builder, and the group platform-engineers, all of which belong to the owner's account. Callers must present valid signed credentials, and unauthenticated requests receive HTTP 403. The ci-deployer role is the only principal allowed to write objects, and it uses short-lived credentials issued per pipeline run. A lifecycle rule deletes objects under nightly/ after 30 days, while stable/ objects are retained indefinitely. To test the configuration, assume the docs-builder role, download a stable archive, and confirm that the same request sent without credentials fails with 403.

This guide describes the bucket acme-cli-builds, which stores the compressed tarballs and zip archives produced by the continuous integration pipeline for a command-line tool. Nightly builds are written to nightly/<date>/ and stable builds to stable/<version>/, and each archive has a detached .asc signature beside it. Public access is allowed on the bucket, and the account-level guardrail is set to permit an anonymous-read policy on this bucket only. Read access is granted by a bucket policy that allows Principal "*" to perform objects:GetObject on every key in the bucket. Callers do not need credentials, and any unauthenticated HTTPS GET for an existing key returns HTTP 200. The ci-deployer role is the only principal allowed to write objects, and it uses short-lived credentials issued per pipeline run. A lifecycle rule deletes objects under nightly/ after 30 days, while stable/ objects are retained indefinitely. To test the configuration, download a stable archive with curl and no credentials, confirm it succeeds, and confirm that an unauthenticated upload attempt fails with 403.

This guide sets up the bucket acme-pkg-repo, which serves as the backing store for a Linux package repository containing .deb and .rpm files plus their metadata. Packages live under dists/ and pool/ for Debian-style layouts and under rpm/<arch>/ for RPM layouts, and the repository metadata is signed with a GPG key held by the release team. Public access is blocked, so the bucket cannot be listed or read by anonymous clients. Read access is given to the IAM roles mirror-sync and fleet-provisioner and to the IAM user repo-admin, all in the owner's account. Package managers on managed hosts obtain credentials through the fleet-provisioner role and send signed requests. A host without those credentials receives HTTP 403 when it requests Packages.gz or repomd.xml. Only repo-admin can write or delete objects, and every metadata update is followed by a re-signing step. To verify, configure one managed host with the role credentials, run a package index refresh, and confirm that the same refresh from an unmanaged host fails.

This guide sets up the bucket acme-pkg-repo, which serves as the backing store for a Linux package repository containing .deb and .rpm files plus their metadata. Packages live under dists/ and pool/ for Debian-style layouts and under rpm/<arch>/ for RPM layouts, and the repository metadata is signed with a GPG key held by the release team. Public access is allowed, so any anonymous client can read objects in the bucket by key. Read access is given to everyone through a bucket policy that allows Principal "*" to perform objects:GetObject on dists/*, pool/*, and rpm/*. Package managers on any host send plain HTTPS requests without credentials or request signing. Any host can therefore request Packages.gz or repomd.xml and receive HTTP 200. Only repo-admin can write or delete objects, and every metadata update is followed by a re-signing step. To verify, run a package index refresh from a host with no cloud credentials, confirm it succeeds, and confirm that an unauthenticated delete request fails.

This guide covers the bucket acme-android-beta, which holds signed .apk and .aab files for pre-release builds of a mobile application. Each build is placed under beta/<build-number>/ along with a manifest.json file that lists the version code, minimum OS level, and checksum. Public access is blocked on the bucket, and object ACLs are disabled so that only policies control access. Read access is granted to the IAM group beta-testers, which contains named accounts for 25 enrolled testers, and to the IAM role release-automation. Testers download builds through the storage console or the command-line client after signing in, and signed requests are checked against the group policy. A request from a person who is not in the group, or from an unauthenticated client, receives HTTP 403. The release-automation role uploads new builds, and removing a tester from the group revokes access immediately. To validate the setup, sign in as a tester and fetch manifest.json, then fetch the same key without signing in and confirm the denial.

This guide covers the bucket acme-android-beta, which holds signed .apk and .aab files for pre-release builds of a mobile application. Each build is placed under beta/<build-number>/ along with a manifest.json file that lists the version code, minimum OS level, and checksum. Public access is allowed on the bucket, and object ACLs are disabled so that only the bucket policy controls access. Read access is granted to anyone on the internet by a bucket policy that allows Principal "*" to perform objects:GetObject on beta/*. Testers download builds with a browser or any HTTP client using the object URL, and no sign-in or request signing is needed. A request from any client, including one with no identity at all, receives HTTP 200 for an existing key. The release-automation role uploads new builds, and removing the bucket policy statement revokes public reads immediately. To validate the setup, fetch manifest.json with curl and no credentials and confirm success, then confirm that an unauthenticated write returns 403.

This guide explains how to store firmware update images for a family of network routers in the bucket acme-device-firmware. Images are organized as models/<model>/<version>/firmware.bin, and each image has a firmware.bin.sig file that devices verify before flashing. Public access is blocked at the bucket level, and the setting cannot be overridden by object-level permissions. Read access is limited to the IAM role update-service, the role factory-flasher, and the user firmware-lead, all within the owner's account. The update-service role is attached to the backend that tells devices which version to install, and it hands out time-limited signed URLs to authorized devices. A client that requests an object key directly without credentials or a valid signed URL receives HTTP 403. Writes are restricted to firmware-lead, and uploads require the object to include a version metadata tag. To verify the configuration, generate a signed URL with the update-service role, confirm the image downloads, and confirm that the bare object URL returns 403.

This guide explains how to store firmware update images for a family of network routers in the bucket acme-device-firmware. Images are organized as models/<model>/<version>/firmware.bin, and each image has a firmware.bin.sig file that devices verify before flashing. Public access is allowed at the bucket level, and the setting is combined with a bucket policy that covers the models/ prefix. Read access is granted to everyone through a bucket policy with Principal "*" and the objects:GetObject action on models/*. The update service tells devices which version to install, and devices then fetch the image directly from the object URL without credentials or a signed URL. A client that requests an object key directly receives HTTP 200 and the file contents. Writes are restricted to firmware-lead, and uploads require the object to include a version metadata tag. To verify the configuration, request the bare object URL with curl, confirm the image downloads, and confirm that its signature file verifies.

This guide configures the bucket acme-sdk-releases, which stores versioned SDK archives for Java, Python, and Go along with source bundles and API reference packages. Objects are named sdk/<language>/<version>/<artifact>, and each release includes a SHA-512 checksum file and a signature file. Public access is blocked, and a bucket policy denies any request that is not made by a principal in the owner's account. Read access is granted to the IAM roles partner-integration and internal-build and to the IAM group sdk-maintainers. Partner organizations that need an SDK receive a named IAM user in the owner's account and must sign every request with that user's credentials. Requests from any other source, including anonymous clients, are rejected with HTTP 403. Only sdk-maintainers can upload or overwrite artifacts, and overwriting an existing version key is blocked by an object-lock retention period. To verify, run cirrus object head on a Java archive using the internal-build role and confirm success, then repeat it anonymously and confirm a 403.

This guide configures the bucket acme-sdk-releases, which stores versioned SDK archives for Java, Python, and Go along with source bundles and API reference packages. Objects are named sdk/<language>/<version>/<artifact>, and each release includes a SHA-512 checksum file and a signature file. Public access is allowed, and a bucket policy permits requests from any source, including anonymous clients. Read access is granted to everyone on the internet by a statement that allows Principal "*" to perform objects:GetObject on sdk/*. Partner organizations and individual developers fetch an SDK with a plain HTTPS GET and do not need an account or credentials. Requests that attempt to write, overwrite, or delete objects are rejected with HTTP 403. Only sdk-maintainers can upload artifacts, and overwriting an existing version key is blocked by an object-lock retention period. To verify, run curl --head on a Java archive with no credentials and confirm an HTTP 200, then confirm that an anonymous overwrite attempt fails.

This guide describes the bucket acme-offline-bundles, which holds large offline installer bundles, typically 2 to 8 GB each, for deployment on isolated networks. Bundles are uploaded with multipart upload and stored under bundles/<product>/<version>/, with a bundle-manifest.json listing the included components and hashes. Public access is blocked on the bucket, and the owner's account policy prevents it from being switched off without an approved change request. Read access is granted to the IAM role deployment-engineers and the role customer-success, plus the named IAM user transfer-agent used by the media-export job. Each principal must send signed requests, and byte-range requests are allowed so that interrupted downloads can resume. An unsigned request for any bundle key returns HTTP 403 regardless of the range header. The deployment-engineers role is also the only one that can upload new bundles. To verify, download the first 1 MB of a bundle with a range request under the customer-success role, and confirm that the same range request without credentials is denied.

This guide describes the bucket acme-offline-bundles, which holds large offline installer bundles, typically 2 to 8 GB each, for deployment on isolated networks. Bundles are uploaded with multipart upload and stored under bundles/<product>/<version>/, with a bundle-manifest.json listing the included components and hashes. Public access is allowed on the bucket, and the owner's account policy permits it through an approved change request recorded for this bucket. Read access is granted to everyone through a bucket policy that allows Principal "*" to perform objects:GetObject on bundles/*. Clients send plain unsigned HTTPS requests, and byte-range requests are allowed so that interrupted downloads can resume. An unsigned request for any bundle key returns HTTP 200, or HTTP 206 when a range header is present. The deployment-engineers role is the only one that can upload new bundles. To verify, download the first 1 MB of a bundle with a range request and no credentials, and confirm that an unauthenticated upload attempt is denied.

This guide sets up the bucket acme-release-archive, which retains installers and artifacts for versions that are out of active support. Objects are stored under archive/<major>/<version>/, and a lifecycle rule moves objects older than 12 months to the infrequent-access storage class. Public access is blocked, and neither the storage class transition nor restore operations change the access rules. Read access is granted to the IAM roles support-engineering and compliance-audit and to the IAM user archive-owner, all in the owner's account. Each of these principals must authenticate, and restores from the cold tier are requested using the same credentials. Anonymous requests to any key, whether archived or restored, return HTTP 403. The archive-owner user is the only principal allowed to write or delete, and deletions require multi-factor authentication. To verify, request a restore of one archived installer as support-engineering, download it after the restore completes, and confirm that the unauthenticated request for the same key returns 403.

This guide sets up the bucket acme-release-archive, which retains installers and artifacts for versions that are out of active support. Objects are stored under archive/<major>/<version>/, and a lifecycle rule moves objects older than 12 months to the infrequent-access storage class. Public access is allowed, and neither the storage class transition nor restore operations change the access rules. Read access is granted to everyone on the internet by a bucket policy that allows Principal "*" to perform objects:GetObject on archive/*. Clients do not need to authenticate, and a restore of a cold-tier object is requested through the console by the owner, after which anyone can download it. Anonymous requests to any restored key return HTTP 200. The archive-owner user is the only principal allowed to write or delete, and deletions require multi-factor authentication. To verify, request a restore of one archived installer as archive-owner, download it with curl and no credentials after the restore completes, and confirm that an unauthenticated delete returns 403.
